claim: DNA methylation, especially CpG methylation at promoter regions, has been generally considered as a potent epigenetic modification that prohibits transcription factor (TF) recruitment, resulting in transcription suppression.
source_text: DNA methylation, especially CpG methylation at promoter regions, has been generally considered as a potent epigenetic modification that prohibits transcription factor (TF) recruitment, resulting in transcription suppression.
evidence_reasoning: This statement reflects established scientific consensus about the general understanding of DNA methylation's role in gene regulation.

claim: Numerous purified TFs exhibit methylated CpG (mCpG)-dependent DNA-binding activities.
source_text: Here, we used a protein microarray-based approach to systematically survey the entire human TF family and found numerous purified TFs with methylated CpG (mCpG)-dependent DNA-binding activities.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by experimental data from protein microarray-based screening described in the manuscript.

claim: Some TFs exhibit specific binding activity to methylated and unmethylated DNA motifs of distinct sequences.
source_text: Interestingly, some TFs exhibit specific binding activity to methylated and unmethylated DNA motifs of distinct sequences.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by experimental observations from protein microarray and EMSA assays presented in the manuscript.

claim: KLF4's mCpG- and CpG-binding activities can be decoupled via site-directed mutagenesis.
source_text: To elucidate the underlying mechanism, we focused on Kruppel-like factor 4 (KLF4), and decoupled its mCpG- and CpG-binding activities via site-directed mutagenesis.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by experimental data from site-directed mutagenesis experiments and subsequent binding assays.

claim: KLF4 binds specific methylated or unmethylated motifs in human embryonic stem cells in vivo.
source_text: Furthermore, KLF4 binds specific methylated or unmethylated motifs in human embryonic stem cells in vivo.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by ChIP-bisulfite sequencing data from H1 human embryonic stem cells presented in the manuscript.

claim: mCpG-dependent TF binding activity is a widespread phenomenon.
source_text: Our study suggests that mCpG-dependent TF binding activity is a widespread phenomenon and provides a new framework to understand the role and mechanism of TFs in epigenetic regulation of gene transcription.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is based on the systematic screening data showing 41 TFs and 6 co-factors with mCpG-dependent binding activity, and inference from these results.

claim: DNA methylation plays an important role in genomic imprinting, X-chromosome inactivation, suppression of transposable elements, and carcinogenesis.
source_text: DNA methylation is an ancient and major epigenetic modification that plays an important role in key biological processes, including genomic imprinting, X-chromosome inactivation, suppression of transposable elements, and carcinogenesis
evidence_reasoning: This statement is supported by citations (Jaenisch and Bird, 2003; Egger et al., 2004; Robertson, 2005; Feinberg, 2007; Reik, 2007) and represents established scientific knowledge.

claim: Methylation of CpG sites at promoter regions is generally considered the hallmark of gene silencing in higher eukaryotes.
source_text: In higher eukaryotes, methylation of CpG sites, especially at promoter regions, is generally considered as the hallmark of gene silencing
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citation (Baylin, 2005) and represents established scientific consensus.

claim: CpG methylation disrupts TF–DNA interactions either directly or indirectly by recruiting sequence-independent methylated DNA-binding proteins.
source_text: The molecular consequence of CpG methylation is generally believed to disrupt TF–DNA interactions either directly (Nan et al., 1998), or indirectly by recruiting sequence-independent methylated DNA-binding proteins that occupy the methylated promoters and compete for the TF binding sites
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by citations (Nan et al., 1998; Boyes and Bird, 1991) and represents established understanding in the field.

claim: MeCP2, MBD1, MBD2, and a few zinc finger proteins have been identified as bona fide methylated DNA-binding proteins.
source_text: So far, only MeCP2, MBD1, MBD2, and a few zinc finger proteins have been identified as bona fide methylated DNA-binding proteins
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by multiple citations (Lewis et al., 1992; Meehan et al., 1989; Filion et al., 2006; Bartke et al., 2010; Bartels et al., 2011; Quenneville et al., 2011; Spruijt et al., 2013).

claim: A total of 154 DNA motifs were selected for the study.
source_text: We selected a total of 154 DNA motifs
evidence_reasoning: This is a direct statement about the experimental design and materials used in the study.

claim: 150 of the 154 methylated motifs (97%) showed significant binding signals to at least one protein on the microarrays.
source_text: Of the 154 methylated motifs examined, 150 (97%) showed significant binding signals to at least one protein on the microarrays
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative result from the protein microarray experiments.

claim: Binding to methylated DNA is prevalent in the in vitro competition assay.
source_text: Of the 154 methylated motifs examined, 150 (97%) showed significant binding signals to at least one protein on the microarrays (median = 8), suggesting binding to methylated DNA is prevalent, at least in this in vitro competition assay
evidence_reasoning: This inference is based on the high percentage (97%) of methylated motifs showing binding signals in the experimental data.

claim: 41 TFs and 6 TF co-factors (3% of all factors examined) showed mCpG-dependent binding activity.
source_text: In addition, 41 TFs and 6 TF co-factors (3% of all factors examined) showed mCpG-dependent binding activity
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative result from the protein microarray screening experiments.

claim: 15% of mCpG-binding proteins showed broad binding activity to over 50% of all methylated motifs tested.
source_text: Among these, 15% showed a broad binding activity to over 50% of all methylated motifs tested, suggesting that these proteins are not sensitive to the sequence context surrounding the mCpG site.
evidence_reasoning: This is based on quantitative analysis of the binding data, with inference about sequence context sensitivity.

claim: ZNF114 and ZNF416 could recognize almost all of the motifs tested in the competition assay.
source_text: For example, two zinc finger TFs, ZNF114 and ZNF416, could recognize almost all of the motifs tested in the competition assay.
evidence_reasoning: This is a specific observation from the protein microarray experiments.

claim: The majority of the 47 mCpG-binding proteins showed mCpG- and sequence-dependent binding activity.
source_text: However, the majority of the 47 mCpG-binding proteins showed mCpG- and sequence-dependent binding activity, with 22 TFs exhibiting binding signaling to fewer than three motifs
evidence_reasoning: This is based on quantitative analysis of the binding patterns observed in the protein microarray experiments.

claim: The mCpG binding activity is widespread among various TF subfamilies including zf-C2H2, Homeobox, bHLH, Forkhead, bZIP, and HMG box subfamilies.
source_text: Notably, the mCpG binding activity is widespread among various TF subfamilies, such as the zf-C2H2, Homeobox, bHLH, Forkhead, bZIP, and HMG box subfamilies
evidence_reasoning: This is based on analysis of the TF subfamily distribution among the identified mCpG-binding proteins.

claim: No TF subfamily was found significantly enriched in the hit list of mCpG-binding proteins.
source_text: no TF subfamily was found significantly enriched in the hit list
evidence_reasoning: This is based on statistical analysis of the TF subfamily distribution shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 5.

claim: There was a significant enrichment for known oncogenes and tumor suppressors among mCpG-binding proteins (10/47; p<0.01).
source_text: consistent with the important role of DNA methylation in the development of cancer (Egger et al., 2004; Reik, 2007), there was a significant enrichment for known oncogenes and tumor suppressors (10/47; p<0.01; hypergeometric model)
evidence_reasoning: This is based on statistical analysis of the functional annotations of identified proteins, with context provided by citations.

claim: There was a significant enrichment for factors involved in tissue development among mCpG-binding proteins (25/47; p<0.015).
source_text: factors involved in tissue development (25/47; p<0.015; hypergeometric model
evidence_reasoning: This is based on statistical analysis of the functional annotations of identified proteins.

claim: Methylation-dependent direct TF–DNA interaction is a widespread phenomenon among various TF subfamilies in humans.
source_text: Together, these results suggest that methylation-dependent direct TF–DNA interaction is a widespread phenomenon among various TF subfamilies in humans.
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference based on the comprehensive screening data showing mCpG-binding activity across multiple TF subfamilies.

claim: 8 of the 11 tested TFs could form a protein–DNA complex with their corresponding methylated motifs, but not with the unmethylated form, as confirmed by EMSA.
source_text: Using an electrophoretic mobility shift assay (EMSA), we confirmed that 8 of the 11 tested TFs could readily form a protein–DNA complex with their corresponding methylated motifs, but not with the unmethylated form
evidence_reasoning: This is a direct result from EMSA validation experiments.

claim: The protein microarray assay has either a 27% false positive rate or higher sensitivity than EMSA.
source_text: This result indicates either a 27% of false positive rate of the protein microarray assay or a higher sensitivity of protein microarray than EMSA.
evidence_reasoning: This inference is based on the validation rate (8/11) observed in EMSA experiments.

claim: The complex formation between TFs and specific DNA motifs requires CpG methylation and is not non-specific.
source_text: While the binding activities to the mCpG-carrying motifs could be readily competed off with the unlabeled mCpG-containing analogs in 10-fold excess, the unmethylated counterparts showed no obvious impact, indicating that the complex formation between these TFs and specific DNA motifs is not non-specific but requires CpG methylation
evidence_reasoning: This conclusion is based on competition EMSA experimental results showing differential effects of methylated vs unmethylated competitors.

claim: HOXA5 and DIDO1 demonstrated dose- and methylation-dependent enhancement of luciferase activity.
source_text: Comparing with the luciferase activity of the negative controls, we found that both HOXA5 and DIDO1 demonstrated dose- and methylation-dependent enhancement of the luciferase activity
evidence_reasoning: This is a direct result from cell-based luciferase assays.

claim: HOXA5 and DIDO1 could specifically bind to methylated promoters and enhance downstream gene transcription.
source_text: Comparing with the luciferase activity of the negative controls, we found that both HOXA5 and DIDO1 demonstrated dose- and methylation-dependent enhancement of the luciferase activity (Figure 1F), indicating that the two TFs could specifically bind to the methylated promoters and enhance the downstream gene transcription.
evidence_reasoning: This inference is based on the luciferase assay results showing methylation-dependent transcriptional activation.

claim: 17 TFs showed binding activity to both methylated and unmethylated DNA motifs.
source_text: we found that 17 TFs showed binding activity to both methylated and unmethylated DNA motifs
evidence_reasoning: This is based on comparison of the current dataset with previous PDI dataset.

claim: Some TFs recognize distinct consensus sequences in methylated vs unmethylated forms.
source_text: Interestingly, some of them recognize distinct consensus sequences in methylated vs unmethylated forms
evidence_reasoning: This observation is based on motif analysis comparing methylated and unmethylated binding sequences.

claim: KLF4 could form a protein–DNA complex with methylated motif M197 (TCCmCpGCCC), but not with its unmethylated form.
source_text: For instance, KLF4 could form a protein–DNA complex with the methylated motif M197 (TCCmCpGCCC), but not with its unmethylated form

source_text: In contrast, methylation on motif M412 (GCTTTTACG) disrupted its interaction with KLF4

claim: TFAP2A, ARID3B, and ZMYM3 show the same dual-specificity phenomenon as KLF4.
source_text: The same phenomenon was confirmed for three additional TFs, namely TFAP2A, ARID3B, and ZMYM3
evidence_reasoning: This is based on EMSA validation experiments for these three TFs.

claim: ARID3B uses either the same DNA-binding domain to interact with both methylated and unmethylated motifs, or binding to one motif inhibits binding to the other.
source_text: For example, the formation of protein–DNA complex between ARID3B and a methylated motif M319 (AAAmCpGCTTCC) could be readily competed off with the unmethylated motif M47 (GTGGGCGAAA) in 10-fold excess, and vice versa (Figure 2E), suggesting that ARID3B either uses the same DNA-binding domain to interact with both motifs, or binding to one motif inhibits binding to the other, presumably via conformational changes or steric hindrance
evidence_reasoning: This inference is based on competition EMSA results showing mutual competition between methylated and unmethylated motifs.

claim: KLF4 may use two different domains to distinguish methylated from unmethylated motifs.
source_text: For instance, KLF4–DNA complex formation with the methylated motif M197 was not affected by adding unmethylated motif M412 in 10-fold excess in the competition assay, suggesting that it may use two different domains to distinguish methylated from unmethylated motifs
evidence_reasoning: This inference is based on competition EMSA results showing independent binding to methylated and unmethylated motifs.

claim: The KD values of ZMYM3, TFAP2A, and KLF4 for their methylated motifs are 460 nM, 399 nM, and 479 nM, respectively.

source_text: On the other hand, the KD values of MBD2b measured against the same motifs are in close range to the three TFs tested (Figure 2—figure supplement 4A), suggesting that these TFs could bind to methylated DNA motifs almost as well as MBD2b
evidence_reasoning: This inference is based on comparison of KD values measured by OIRD for the TFs and MBD2b.

source_text: Intriguingly, KLF4 encodes a classic zf-C2H2 domain, a truncated and a full zf-H2C2 domain at its very C-terminus

source_text: Similarly, KLF4 truncation showed no binding activity to methylated motif M197 (CCmCpGCC), but still maintained its binding activity to the unmethylated motif M412 (TACpGCC; Figure 3—figure supplement 3), indicating that the C2H2 zinc finger in KLF4 mediates KLF4's interaction with unmethylated motif M412.
evidence_reasoning: This inference is based on EMSA results with truncated KLF4 protein showing differential binding to methylated vs unmethylated motifs.
